s: Distributes a single incoming message to multiple downstream subscribers or destinations based on subscription rules.
w: Receives a message or event and fans it out to all registered consumers in parallel. Implementation ranges from Pub/Sub topic fan-out to custom services that maintain subscriber lists and deliver via HTTP, queue, or WebSocket push. Each subscriber receives an independent copy. Fan-out decouples producers from knowing about all downstream consumers; new consumers register without producer changes.
use: Event broadcast to multiple services (order.created -> email + analytics + fraud)
Real-time notification distribution to multiple channels (push + email + in-app)
Multi-consumer data feeds (one telemetry stream -> monitoring + warehouse + alerting)
Webhook distribution to registered third-party endpoints
avoid: Competing-consumer patterns where only one worker should process each message (use queue)
Low-volume point-to-point communication (direct API call is simpler)
Ordered processing across subscribers (each subscriber gets independent order)

props.subscriber_count: Number of downstream consumers per event type

size.messages_per_sec: Depends on implementation; Pub/Sub handles ~100k+ per topic

pat.d: Fan-out IS the mechanism enabling decoupled event consumers.

pits: Slow subscriber creating backpressure on fast ones - each subscriber should be independently buffered
Missing subscriber failure handling - dead-letter or retry per subscriber, not globally
tips: Fan-out vs fan-in: fan-out = one-to-many distribution, fan-in = many-to-one aggregation
Pub/Sub topics and SNS are the managed fan-out implementations to reference
